answer: A seat is proven by its postmark. One address each; each epoch the seeded words form the second line of a hand-addressed card posted to the ledger's PO box by 17:00. The clerk photographs the cancellation: date, sorting-centre code. That dull grey band, no opal fire, is the signal the ledger trusts; no desk printer makes one. Cards sharing a postmark hour or a stamp batch fold into one vote, losing 25,000 POA each. A clone needs an address, $1.60 postage, two days of transit: 1,000 seats burn $1,600 an epoch. An oasis fools the eye at a mile; a postmark is the wet footprint you follow.
